facts.statement: A random split is appropriate only if its sampling interpretation matches the intended evaluation; dependent grouped or time-ordered data can require different boundaries.
Keep observations from a common evaluation group entirely on one side of the boundary, and keep time-ordered training observations earlier than the intended later evaluation observations.
Implement the supplied group membership with sets and assert that training and validation group intersections are empty.
For a time boundary, select training observations before the cutoff and later evaluation observations under the stated scenario, and check the timestamp inequalities.
Calculate each partition’s target outcome count divided by its partition total to report the population actually evaluated.
Write assert predicate checks for the declared valid, boundary and failure cases; a false predicate raises AssertionError during ordinary non-optimized execution.

practice.objective: Implement a learner-defined Python function that partitions supplied list observations according to a declared group-based or time-based deployment scenario. Justify the boundaries, calculate each partition's target proportion, and verify the deliverable with learner-written assertions and supplied unit-test fixtures. Write any imports required by the supplied fixture interface.
practice.success: The function assigns observations according to the stated scenario. Group-based partitions keep each group wholly on one side and have empty group-set intersections. Time-based partitions satisfy the declared cutoff and later-interval inequalities, including cutoff equality cases. Each nonempty partition reports its target count divided by its total. Assertions pass for valid fixtures and raise AssertionError for declared violations during ordinary non-optimized execution; supplied unit-test fixtures confirm the same deliverable.

live_code.required_skill: Partition list observations using scenario-specific predicates, represent group membership with sets, calculate target proportions, and author assertions that verify the declared boundaries.
allowed_syntax: import and from ... import for required supplied fixture dependencies
set literals, set comprehensions, and set()
dictionary literals and supplied observation field access
membership tests with in and not in
Boolean operators and, or, and not
integer, floating-point, string, and Boolean literals
calls to the supplied fixture and unit-test interfaces
live_code.starter_state_intent: Supply separate group and time fixtures, a declared scenario contract, and an existing test harness without completed partition logic. Use orders A and B from G1 and C from G2 for the group fixture; use supplied order timestamps and a declared cutoff for the time fixture. Include target outcomes, valid cases, cutoff boundary cases, and deliberately invalid assignments. The learner writes the function, any required imports, and assertions.
live_code.observable_success: Returned partitions satisfy the supplied assignment expectations. Group-set intersections are empty where required; timestamp predicates enforce the exact declared boundaries. Reported target proportions match fixture counts for each nonempty partition. Learner-written assertions detect overlapping groups and invalid time assignments, and the supplied tests confirm valid and boundary behavior.
